curation.notes: Dual-beam single-trap optical tweezers (bead in trap + streptavidin bead on suction micropipette) hold a 6,256 bp lambda DNA tether in Xenopus high-speed egg extract (metaphase or interphase; mock, ASF1-, H1.8- or condensin-depleted) and track chromatin fiber compaction at ~1.5 pN and force-induced disassembly at 15 pN in force-feedback mode. Fluorescence imaging was only used to test extract activity on sperm nuclei, not correlatively.

evidence.snippet: The DNA was deposited on 2 µm polystyrene beads (Spherotech) coated with anti-dig antibody.

The 6.2 kb DNA tether was amplified by PCR from lambda phage genomic DNA using a 5′-biotinylated primer (5’-biotin-gaacagacagaggacgccg), and a 5′-digoxigenin labeled primer (5’-dig-ggccatgttgttgctgtatgc) (IDT).

entities.name: Xenopus laevis high-speed egg extract (metaphase / interphase)

evidence.snippet: We developed a physiological, cell-free system using high-speed Xenopus egg extracts and optical tweezers to investigate real-time mitotic chromatin fiber formation and force-induced disassembly on single DNA molecules.
For condensin, 10 μg each of affinity-purified antibodies against CAP-E, CAP-G, and CAP-D3 was coupled to 100 μL protein A Dynabeads (20).
For H1.8, 50 μg affinity-purified anti-H1M antibody was coupled to 200 μL protein A Dynabeads (Thermo Fisher) as described (7).
Depletion of the core histone chaperone ASF1, which inhibits nucleosome assembly, decreased the final degree of metaphase fiber compaction by 29%

solution.buffer: EB buffer + high-speed egg extract (1:1) + 1/20 vol energy mix
solution.notes: EB buffer composition before 1:1 mixing with extract; energy mix = 150 mM creatine phosphate, 20 mM ATP, 2 mM EGTA, 20 mM MgCl2.
